This is pretty good advice. It can be better though. For instance, what may not be known is that if the wife starts contributing to the trust, (which is reasonable if the intention is to pass property to children), that protection is gone.

A better bet is to create an LLC for your personal assets and a C-Corp for shared assets. This way there is a legally defined separation of duty. But you need to form the LLC and C-Corp BEFORE you get married.

I don't recommend a trust because once you put something into a trust it's nearly impossible to get it out again without a court order. Whereas, with an LLC you can still dissolve the corporation and get your assets back.

With a C-Corp, you can distribute inheritance BEFORE you die. For instance, the family farm. Your kids are working on it and deserve ownership of it while you are still alive. So, you allocate shares to them when they are deserving.

A C-Corp isn't necessarily a way to dodge taxes. But the taxes will essentially be classified as a "Dividend" and in most cases, you are given a reduced rate, or exempt, on dividends if you play your cards right.

You might also want to look into an S-Corp. The difference between a C-Corp and an S-Corp is the tax structure.

In a C-Corp, the corporation itself is responsible for handling its taxes. In a S-Corp, the shareholders are responsible for handling the taxes of the portion they control.

An S-Corp might be a safer bet if you are worried about double taxation, but, like I said, play your cards right and it's not really an issue.
